notes.note: All 930 actual units across 29 chapters were inventoried before source review. Every original source reference, anchor, word and metadata field is retained. The supplied source edition’s editorial and running-text statements and pending specialist checks remain provenance only; this tracker does not claim to have performed them. This inventory baseline records all units as pending, with zero completed source verses or pairs; any subsequent initial curated review is recorded separately in the tracker.
Continuation units: 0. Chapters with missing numeric verse numbers: 2. Exact ordered lists are in inventory.json; do not import another edition’s names or numbering.

Keep actual missing units 11–16 and 18–23 absent; unit 24 remains only Sala. Preserve every supplied name and relationship, including eight Japheth sons and differences from Genesis. Do not infer repeated Ana or Daison identities across different stated roles. Units 24 and 52 remain pending.

Preserve Arson/Jemouel, Zara and Charmi/Achar forms, Jirameel/Aram and Jeremeel, Gazouba-a-wife wording, twenty-three versus sixty cities, Eseron death and Abia birth order, childless Salad and Jether, Sosan daughters and Jochel marriage, and the actual father-of-place relationships. Jadai’s independent branch at 47 remains pending.

Preserve David’s differing Hebron child/mother names, six Hebron sons, seven years six months and thirty-three years, four by Bersabee and the following nine, repeated Jerusalem names, Themar, all royal generations and differing Matthew forms, Jechonia-asir, Salathiel, and all supplied descendant counts.

Preserve actual Sarathi, Aitam, Saour/Aoda/Thoada, Igabes’s naming and knowledge prayer, craftsman Joab without equating him with Zeruiah’s son, Caleb son of Jephonne, uncertain His son and His wife wording, ephrath abak and abedirin athoukiin without glosses, sixteen sons and three daughters, half of Sosim, the supplied five-city count with four named entries, named Hezekiah-era settlers, and five hundred Simeonites led by Jesi’s four sons. Units 3,8,16,17,18,19,20 remain pending.

Keep the actual chapter through unit 41: the Levite and priestly material at 27–41 belongs here. Preserve the firstborn-blessing distinction, all named ancestry, actual place forms, Joatham/Jeroboam enrollment, 44,760 warriors, 5,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys, 100,000 human lives, Phaloch/Thaglathphalnasar, Joanan/Joanas, repeated priestly names, and Josadak’s deportation wording. No familiar twenty-six-unit division is substituted.

Preserve the actual Greek chapter division: this chapter has 66 units, not the familiar 81-unit Christian chapter division. Names and successive-son wording are retained exactly; no different editions supply missing entries or alter the clan allocations. Manasseh and half-Manasseh are distinguished in 6:47/56.
The retained bounded father-role connection preserves Samuel's sons Sani and Abia in 6:13 and Joel son of Samuel in 6:18. No Sani=Joel or Abia=Abijah identity equation is credited.

Moocha's sister and wife roles remain as supplied; Malecheth's 'his sister', the son-chain antecedents, Ozan/Seera wording, the resettlement pronouns, Sosek's brother phrase and the Netophati residence antecedent are not independently resolved. Retained local context links explain actual grammatical continuity without establishing a new parentage, gender, agent or identity.

The Ner-Kish-Saul parallels are bounded to the exact shared genealogy and Jonathan/Melchisoue/Amminadab names; Asabal and Isbaal are not equated. Esel/Asel, six-son figures and actual printed name lists are preserved without supplying a missing name or harmonizing another list.

Only supported retained source-target pairs receive completion credit. 7:12 and 7:19 remain empty/pending with zero credit. Full-book inventory, inherited metadata and technical pin checks are not newly completed review. Independent AI peer review is pending after this author freeze.

notes: Chapter 12 contains 41 actual source units in this edition; none were renumbered to a familiar forty-verse arrangement.
Saul’s whole-house death notice, Samuel’s armour-bearer notice, distinct trophy locations, sons, and burial objects are preserved.

The warrior comparisons preserve three hundred wounded versus eight hundred slain, sword versus spear, barley versus lentils, differently introduced actors, thirty versus three, and distinct royal appointments. No independent name-equivalence or identity equation is claimed.

Bare names in the continuing warrior and helper rosters are connected to explicit same-chapter grammatical headings or summaries; no deed, clan identity, or ancestry absent from the source is invented.
Ark route wording, the explicit hand-on-ark cause, calf movement, different instruments, and each householder’s source form remain distinct.

David’s order to burn abandoned gods is related to Deuteronomy’s command without claiming the execution of the order was narrated. Pear-tree and place-of-weeping instructions retain each passage’s actual wording.
